pediatricPearls: Use pediatric dosing of medications or electrical therapy for a pediatric patient < 37 kg and as defined by the PEDIA Tape.
Avoid intubation of the pediatric patient when possible. OPA/NPA is preferred.
Children compensate well initially but decompensate quickly with little warning.
Most pediatric cardiac arrests are due to respiratory compromise.

pl1: BLS Foreign Body Airway Obstruction evaluation / removal
Place NPA and/or OPA and ventilate with BVM
Oxygen, including passive apneic oxygenation 25 lpm with NC
pl4: IV / IO access as appropriate for patient condition
pl5: Direct laryngoscopy Foreign Body Airway Obstruction evaluation / removal.
All advanced airway procedures will include passive apneic oxygenation when possible
Continuous ETCO is mandatory for all intubations
Push dose Epinephrine or Norepinephrine prior to intubation
Direct laryngoscopy intubation with Gum Bougie
Surgical cricothyroidotomy if patient > 10 years of age
pl6: Use Airway Management Checklist for all Rapid Sequence Inductions
